However this risk is manageable since there are several other suitable parcels currently available in the Port, and that have been available for many years. There does not currently seem to be a high demand for such parcels and therefore no significant risk that they will all be taken in the next several Page45 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version years. Nonetheless, Aptamus is considering offering a nominal annual payment to reserve the land during T-RICH project development over the next few years. When it is time to enter into a long-term lease for the land, Aptamus expects to pay a base lease rate plus a “Wharfage Rate” which is “applicable on commodities loaded to or unloaded from vessels in a bulk state.” See the Tampa Port Authority’s Terminal Tariff No. 14 publication on their website.15 The base rate will be negotiated based on the location of the parcel and market conditions at the time of negotiations. Aptamus has some experience with this since its affiliate OSG holds a long-term lease on a smaller parcel in the port on which its fleet-support warehouse is situated. Regarding the “Wharfage Rate”, Port Tampa Bay currently has no published rate applicable to CO since it has never been shipped by marine vessel in 2 the U.S. before. So along with the base lease rate negotiations, this wharfage rate will also be negotiated. But the port does have a published rate for anhydrous ammonia which is mentioned elsewhere in this report as being a similar cargo to CO in some ways. This report assumes that rate will also apply to CO 2 2 and assumes that the price charged for anhydrous ammonia, at $0.417 per short ton (2,000 lbs), will also apply to CO . 2 The following table summarizes the path to commissioning the hub in terms of land “acquisition”: Table 3.6: Summary of the Land Acquisition Process Item Description Timeline  Approximately five years until commissioning.  Aptamus may consider paying a nominal payment to reserve the land for several of those years.  Five years may be necessary to allow area emitters to commit to carbon capture and then take several years for the EPC process. Critical Items  Another future tenant secures the land before Aptamus is ready to make a long-term commitment to it. Decision Points  Aptamus needs to have a long-term commitment from a Florida emitter of CO before it can commit to a long-term land lease 2 agreement.
